item.title: GraphQL-core: Denial of service via quadratic complexity in the OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged validation rule
item.description: Score 68/100 HIGH — CVSS 7.5 — ### Summary The `OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged` validation rule can be driven into quadratic — and in the worst case `O(n²·m²)` — running time by a small, highly compressible query. A single 364 KB document can occupy one CPU core for over five minutes during *validation*, before any resolver runs. B. Full analysis, Sigma/YARA rules, IOCs, Attack Chain by CYBERDUDEBIVASH SENTINEL APEX v4.0.

item.title: toml-node: Uncontrolled resource consumption (CPU DoS) via unbounded-length integer literals in toml.parse()
item.description: Score 61/100 MEDIUM — CVSS 7.5 — ### Summary `toml.parse()` converts integer literals (hex, octal, binary, and decimal) to `BigInt` without first bounding the length of the digit sequence. Since `BigInt(string)` construction from a very long numeric string runs in super-linear time, a single small, well-formed TOML document contain. Full analysis, Sigma/YARA rules, IOCs, Attack Chain by CYBERDUDEBIVASH SENTINEL APEX v4.0.

item.title: GraphQL-core: Denial of service via comment tokens bypassing the parser's max_tokens limit
item.description: Score 61/100 MEDIUM — CVSS 7.5 — ### Summary The parser's `max_tokens` limit — the documented defence against oversized GraphQL documents — did not count comment tokens. A document padded with comments could therefore pass a `max_tokens` check of any size while still allocating one `Token` object per comment, all of which stay reac.
